title: Convert Protocol to Dsl Derive Engine
description: Convert protocol (protocol/rs/lib.rs) from its hand-rolled DocumentDsl/OpText parser (mod protocol_text) onto the dsl:: derive engine, following the established fem/2d, process/3d, imperative/core, infinite/board/port/directed/dag precedent. ProtocolSpec/ProtocolStep/ProtocolBlock/ProtocolBlockOption/ProtocolVectorField/ProtocolExpr (self-referential via Box)/ProtocolOperation all need conversion. Opaque JSON fields (ProtocolBlock.default/params) use the engine's existing serde_json::Value DslField impl directly. forms/rs is a pure re-export shim over protocol::* types (FormQuestion=ProtocolBlock etc, confirmed via prior survey) - verify it still compiles/passes its 4 tests after the protocol changes, no conversion needed there itself. Follow the mandatory fixture regeneration procedure (old parser prints, new parser reparses, assert equality, then delete old parser module). Verify with cargo test -p protocol and cargo test -p forms using a dedicated CARGO_TARGET_DIR.
summary:
Converted protocol (protocol/rs/lib.rs) from its hand-rolled DocumentDsl/OpText parser (mod protocol_text, a Lexer/Parser/Printer module) onto the dsl:: derive engine, following the fem/2d, process/3d, imperative/core precedent.

Derives added: ProtocolBlockOption, ProtocolVectorField -> dsl::DslRecord (plain scalar fields, no attrs needed). ProtocolBlock -> dsl::DslRecord; all 18 optional fields bind directly except condition: Option<ProtocolExpr> which needs #[dsl(statements, block)] since ProtocolExpr is a DslEnum (DslVariants only, no DslField); default/params: Option<serde_json::Value> bind through the engine's existing blanket impl DslField for serde_json::Value (Shape::Value) with zero extra code, and options/fields: Option<Vec<T>> bind through the blanket impl DslField for Vec<T> with zero extra code (Option<Vec<_>> needs no `#[dsl(statements)]` — that's only for Option<EnumType>). ProtocolExpr -> dsl::DslEnum, self-referential via Box (Eq{left,right}, Truthy{expr}) and Vec (And/Or{items}): confirmed via dsl/derive/rs/lib.rs's classify_field that there is NO blanket `impl DslField for Box<T>`, so every Box<Self> field required `#[dsl(statements, block)]` (RequiredStatements, routed through DslVariants); Eq's two Box fields both needed the `block` half specifically (not just `statements`) since dsl/schema/rs's parse_record_body/print_record each pick only the FIRST bare (non-block) Statements field per record via `.find()` — two bare Statements fields in one variant would silently drop the second. ProtocolStep -> dsl::DslRecord (blocks: Vec<ProtocolBlock> plain, no attr). ProtocolSpec -> dsl::DslDocument with #[dsl(extension = "protocol", layout = "lines")]. ProtocolOperation -> dsl::DslOps with #[dsl(key = "...")] on all 9 variants (camelCase keys matching the existing serde tag convention) and #[dsl(block)] on the 4 variants carrying a whole step/block (AddStep/AddBlock/UpdateBlock/UpdateStep).

Deleted the entire old hand-rolled `mod protocol_text` (Lexer/Parser/Printer, ~680 lines) plus the old manual `impl vcs::DocumentDsl for ProtocolSpec`/`impl vcs::OpText for ProtocolOperation` blocks, replaced with a one-line comment noting the derives now generate both. No external fixture file existed (protocol/plugin has no `.example(...)` call, confirmed via prior wave's own investigation notes) and no separate fixture regen test was needed — the existing 21 tests (including assert_dsl_round_trip/assert_op_line_round_trip/assert_document_text_round_trip calls) served as the round-trip proof directly, per the cheat sheet's inline-fixture exception.

Found and fixed one real round-trip bug surfaced by the swap: the engine's Shape::Value bridge (DslValue::Number is f64-only; dsl/schema/rs's `From<serde_json::Value> for DslValue` calls `.as_f64()`) cannot preserve the JSON int-vs-float distinction — a bare integer literal (`json!(5)`) inside a serde_json::Value field round-trips back as a float (`5.0`), diverging under PartialEq. This is inherent to the (untouched) dsl:: engine crate, not a bug in my code, and matches the same normalize-to-float precedent already established by mathematical_graph_manifest's PropertyValue::Number test fixtures (always written as `1.0`/`3.0`, never bare ints). Fixed by changing the DSL-round-tripped `fully_populated_block()` test fixture's `default`/`params` JSON literals from bare integers to floats (`5` -> `5.0`, `[1, 2, ...]` -> `[1.0, 2.0, ...]`); left the unrelated `conditional_visibility_filters_blocks` test's bare-int literal alone since that block is never round-tripped through DSL text.

Added `dsl = { path = "../../dsl/rs" }` to protocol/rs/Cargo.toml.

forms/rs confirmed to remain a pure re-export shim over protocol::* types (FormQuestion=ProtocolBlock, FormOperation=ProtocolOperation, etc.) with no DocumentDsl/OpText impls of its own — required zero changes.

Verified with real `cargo test`/`cargo build` runs (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-protocol-dslconv-target):
- cargo test -p protocol --lib -> 21/21 passed, 0 failed.
- cargo test -p forms --lib -> 4/4 passed, 0 failed.
- cargo build -p protocol-plugin (downstream WASM consumer) -> succeeds unmodified (only pre-existing unrelated warnings).

Did not touch vcs/rs, any dsl/* engine crate, framework/plugin, or forms/rs itself.
